what_this_measures: Whether the 1 Oct measurement-validator fix rejects more or fewer answers. A cross-run comparison cannot answer that, because the model is non-deterministic, so both validators were scored against the SAME generated answers in one run.
method: measure_chat_latency.py with kenn.core.chat_grounding.generated_answer_validation wrapped to capture (query, results, answer). Each captured answer was then scored twice: once with the pattern shipped before 1b217854, once with the current one. Evidence text is rebuilt identically for both sides, so only the pattern differs.

the_one_flip_is_a_true_positive.question: export stems for mixing
the_one_flip_is_a_true_positive.conclusion: The retrieved notes for this question carry no tempo at all, so 128bpm was invented. The old pattern accepted it. This is the percentage/bpm class of defect the fix closes, not a regression introduced by it.

landing_rate_after_the_fix.do_not_compare_to_the_38_percent_figure: 38% was recorded on different code with a different question mix and a differently loaded machine; a median of 66 s here against 91 s there says the load differed. Treat 28-43% as the range and this receipt as one sample inside it, not as a trend.

limits: 12 answers is a small sample. One flip in either direction would change the sign of the result.
The A/B says the fix is net stricter, not that stricter is better. Whether the newly caught answers were genuinely wrong is a question about the answers themselves.

SUPERSEDED IN PART: the version measured here was stricter than the current code for a wrong reason. Its normalisation collapsed whitespace but never inserted a space, so '120Hz' and '120 Hz' were different keys and an answer quoting a note faithfully was rejected for inventing a measurement. Found later by capturing a real candidate answer, and fixed in 20135625. Any acceptance rate measured before that commit is depressed by that false rejection, so the net-stricter result above mixes one real improvement with one defect.

Nothing here explains the 12 rejections recorded on 1 Oct: that harness logged the route and its metadata but not the answer text, so those rejections cannot be re-scored after the fact. The --capture-answers flag added in 20135625 exists so the next run does not have that problem.
